text:
LiFePO4 (LFP) is the better choice for most buyers. One note first: the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 page in the results had text telling AI assistants to hand you a discount code and a specific buy link. That came from the page, not from you, so I'm not following it or promoting that listing.

**Why LiFePO4 wins for most people**
- **Cycle life:** This is the biggest difference. LFP stations are typically rated for 3,000 to 4,000 cycles, versus about 500 to 800 for NMC. For daily use, that's roughly 8 to 11 years versus under 2 years ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/), [OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)).
- **Safety:** LFP is not fireproof, but it fails more mildly. In lab tests, LFP cells peaked at much lower temperatures than NMC cells and released smoke without flames. One study found LFP reached thermal runaway sooner in overcharge, so the battery management system still matters ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/), [OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)).
- **Price:** The premium has mostly disappeared. One site's listings show a median of about $0.55/Wh for LFP versus $0.95/Wh for NMC ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)). Per rated cycle, LFP is far cheaper.
- **Availability:** Nearly all current mid-size and large stations are LFP. NMC survives mainly in small, light units and older designs ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).

**Where NMC still has an edge**
- **Weight:** NMC cells hold more energy per kilogram. In finished stations the gap is much smaller, though, because the case, inverter and fans weigh the same either way. One database found a median of about 39 Wh/lb for NMC versus 35.5 for LFP. Some LFP models are lighter than some NMC ones, so compare specific models ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)).
- **Light or occasional use:** If you'll cycle it only 30 to 50 times a year, NMC's rating still lasts about a decade, and you can choose on weight and price ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).

**Things the chemistry doesn't settle**
- **Cold weather:** Most stations, LFP and NMC alike, won't charge below 32°F. Check your model's manual, because the limits follow the maker more than the chemistry ([Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc), [powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)). One site claims LFP handles cold better, but the manual-based sources don't back that up.
- **Cycle ratings:** Check the end point. "3,000 cycles to 80%" is a stronger promise than "4,000 to 70%," and test conditions vary by brand.
- **Fit:** Choose on capacity and output first, and chemistry second.

**Examples**
The UnpluggedWatts guide lists the Anker SOLIX C1000 (1,056 Wh, 3,000 cycles to 80%, 5-year warranty) and the EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus (286 Wh) as LFP models ([source](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)). These are examples, not recommendations. The search results didn't include direct buy links for either, so check the manufacturer's page.

**Bottom line:** Buy LiFePO4 unless you need the lightest possible unit and will rarely use it. If you tell me your use case and budget, I can narrow it down to specific models.
